field_checks.summary: Primary XML/PDF and final activity records were reviewed. Table 2 is represented as 26 numeric inhibition-circle rows plus 10 dash exclusions, and MIC/Figure 9 rows are present. Blocking failure: three Figure 5/xml:p:39 stability rows are field-misbound. The source says 23.78 ± 0.29 and 22.56 ± 0.59 are Listeria monocytogenes UV-control/80-min values, and 14.14 ± 0.39 is Escherichia coli after 90 min UV; the final instead assigns the first two to Escherichia coli and labels the 14.14 ± 0.39 row as thermal 100 C for 60 min.

Database layer preserved the release boundary: 5 DBAASP/Codex fallback rows remain unresolved_record, no source_verified records are claimed, linked authoritative DBAASP/merged row counts are zero, and authoritative_dbaasp_ingest_ready is false. No final object contains both plain one-letter sequence and sequence_length, so there was no residue-count object to validate.

All six paper-final JSON files exist in the packet final mirror and are byte-identical. Blocking failure: both final materials_manifest.json mirrors still list two open_rework_ticket_ids, while live rework responses and the current packet gate report zero open tickets. The current strict acceptance artifact also reports open_rework_ticket_count 0, so a current final record is internally stale against live packet state.

Mechanism ontology boundaries are preserved. The repaired mechanism record has 3 claims, zero direct_mechanism claims, and empty direct_assay_types. SDS/permeability wording is retained as inferred/discussion context rather than promoted to membrane-potential or dye-permeability assay evidence.

Paper identity was source-confirmed as PMC11897483, PMID 40078294, DOI 10.3389/fphar.2025.1530043, Frontiers in Pharmacology 2025, title matching the G7 bacteriocin P7 study. Entity linkage to bacteriocin P7 and Bacillus velezensis G7 is source-supported, but database authority linkage remains unresolved because local authoritative DBAASP/merged rows are absent.

Path readability and locator-base resolution passed for the required source, packet, work, final, worker-log, and report surfaces; the locator index contains 197 locators, and final source locators resolve at base locator level. Blocking failure remains because locator presence did not preserve correct field binding for xml:p:39/Figure 5 rows; target species and treatment condition are wrong despite valid locators.

Fallback release boundary is preserved: fallback DBAASP rows are not marked authoritative and authoritative_dbaasp_ingest_ready is false. Recursive-authority boundary fails because the current final review and strict acceptance artifact claim publication_grade true and p39 activity-surface contract pass while independent source review finds p39 target/condition field mismatches.

Two intended cautions are preserved: unlinked fallback database rows and the hemolysis threshold discrepancy between results/discussion. A new hard source conflict remains: p39/Figure 5 final activity rows bind UV values to the wrong target/condition, so the current accepted_with_cautions status is not scientifically source-reviewable.

Primary XML has no supplementary-material elements, staged source and packet supplementary directories are present but empty, supplementary index has zero files, supplementary text has zero rows, supplementary tables has zero tables, archive manifest has no archive members, and worker-3 supplementary evidence reviewed those empty staged surfaces.

Toxicity coverage is source-reviewed for chicken erythrocyte hemolysis: methods identify domestic chicken blood and the Figure 10A panel shows exact labels 0.8193, 3.7988, and 10.949 percent for MIC, 2MIC, and 4MIC. Prose threshold rows from p49 and p57 are preserved as approximate cautions. No broader mammalian cytotoxicity or selectivity-index source surface was found.

blocking_findings.reason: Final activity_toxicity_evidence.json incorrectly binds three xml:p:39/Figure 5 stability values. The source states that Listeria monocytogenes has control 23.78 ± 0.29 and 22.56 ± 0.59 after 80 min UV irradiation, while Escherichia coli has 14.14 ± 0.39 after 90 min UV irradiation. The final records instead assign 23.78 ± 0.29 and 22.56 ± 0.59 to Escherichia coli and label 14.14 ± 0.39 as thermal treatment at 100 C for 60 min. The current source_review_audit and strict acceptance artifact report the p39 surface and publication gate as passed around this field mismatch.

Set 23.78 ± 0.29 and 22.56 ± 0.59 to Listeria monocytogenes UV-control and UV 80-min contexts, or exclude them with a source-backed rationale if not recordable.
Set 14.14 ± 0.39 to Escherichia coli UV 90-min context, or exclude it with a source-backed rationale; do not label it thermal 100 C for 60 min unless a separate source value supports that row.
Update paper and packet final activity mirrors and ensure downstream source_review_audit and strict acceptance checks validate target, value, unit, and condition together.
